description: Triage threshold modifiers based on treatment regimen — applied on top of COSTaRS base rules
source: NCCN Guidelines; ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines; ASCO Clinical Practice Guidelines

modifiers.note: FN protocol activated — 14-day cytotoxic window applies

immunotherapy.note: irAE module activated — lower thresholds for immune-mediated symptoms

modifiers.rationale: Diarrhea Grade ≥2 with immunotherapy = suspect immune-mediated colitis
modifiers.citation: NCCN Management of Immunotherapy-Related Toxicities v1.2024; Schneider BJ et al. JCO 2021

modifiers.rationale: Any new dyspnea with immunotherapy = suspect pneumonitis until proven otherwise
modifiers.citation: NCCN irAE v1.2024; Postow MA et al. NEJM 2018

modifiers.rationale: Fatigue with immunotherapy — screen for thyroiditis and hypophysitis
Grade ≥2 rash with immunotherapy — immune-mediated dermatitis; steroids may be needed

drug_specific_rules.citation: NCCN Kidney Cancer; Sorafenib prescribing information

drug_specific_rules.note: Grade 1 EGFR-TKI rash is expected (80% of patients) — not clinically urgent without infection signs
drug_specific_rules.citation: NCCN NSCLC; Lacouture ME et al. JCO 2010

drug_specific_rules.note: CDK4/6 inhibitor-associated diarrhea — higher baseline rate; Grade 2 warrants loperamide adjustment
drug_specific_rules.citation: NCCN Breast Cancer; FDA prescribing information CDK4/6

modifiers.note: Head/neck radiation — mucositis Grade 2+ warrants earlier intervention
modifiers.citation: NCCN Head and Neck Cancers; MASCC/ISOO Guidelines 2014

modifiers.note: Radiation dermatitis — any open sore in radiation field warrants same-day evaluation
Radiation pneumonitis — typically 4-12 weeks post chest RT; any new dyspnea in this window = routine minimum
modifiers.citation: NCCN NSCLC; Marks LB et al. Int J Radiat Oncol 2010

modifiers.note: Joint pain (arthralgia) is common with AI/fulvestrant — Grade 2 warrants review but not urgent
modifiers.citation: NCCN Breast Cancer; ASCO AI management guidelines

modifiers.note: Any fever within 30 days post CAR-T = possible CRS — EMERGENCY. CRS can be fatal without tocilizumab.
modifiers.citation: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas; Lee DW et al. Biol Blood Marrow Transplant 2019

modifiers.note: New neurologic symptoms within 30 days post CAR-T = possible ICANS — EMERGENCY.
modifiers.citation: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas; ASTCT Consensus Grading 2019

modifiers.note: Any fever within 30 days post SCT = FN protocol. Extended window vs standard chemo.
Diarrhea post allo-SCT = consider GvHD — urgent evaluation regardless of grade
modifiers.citation: NCCN Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation; Zeiser R, Blazar BR. NEJM 2017
